# Tagcast 1.9.7

Tagcast 1.9.7 adds reviewed iBroadcast trash emptying, improves upload handling,
and brings a quieter artist-discovery section and readable update notes.

## Review and empty the iBroadcast trash

- Open **Settings → Data → Review iBroadcast trash…** to see the current trash.
  Opening Settings alone does not read or empty it.
- Review the tracks, tick the acknowledgement and confirm once more before
  emptying the entire trash. Reviews show 50 tracks per page, with a local limit
  of 10,000 tracks.
- Tagcast checks for library changes before showing the review and again before
  sending the request. An unchanged current library is reused; a changed or
  unknown revision requires a fresh download. A changed trash review is blocked.
- After emptying, Tagcast reads the library back to confirm the result. This
  full read can take a while for a large library; the progress text explains it.
  For an unchanged loaded library, the complete review-and-empty flow now needs
  one full library download rather than three.
- Change history and export retain the result. An uncertain response is checked
  without automatically sending the request again.

**Emptying is not permanent deletion.** iBroadcast moves these files to
**Unavailable Files** in its Track Dashboard, where they may still count toward
storage. Tagcast does not perform the separate permanent-deletion step or touch
local music files.

## Better upload handling

- Recent accepted and uncertain upload outcomes are remembered within the same
  account/upload session, protecting them from being sent again while the remote
  MD5 list catches up. The guard clears on disconnect, session replacement,
  disabling uploads or restarting Tagcast; it is not a permanent upload log.
- Immediately before sending the first file, Tagcast checks the remote MD5 list
  again and skips reviewed files that are now present. If that check fails,
  no audio is sent.
- If iBroadcast reports a storage limit, Tagcast stops the upload queue rather
  than sending every remaining file. Earlier results are still checked, and
  uncertain uploads are never automatically retried.

## Similar music alongside the artist biography

- **Discover similar music** becomes the **Similar in your library** disclosure,
  beside **About this artist**. The source label follows the results: **Last.fm**
  or **Your library**. **Refresh suggestions** sits inside the open section.
- Opening the section explicitly starts discovery. Returning with Back can
  restore completed results without another request; visiting a new artist does
  not automatically contact Last.fm.
- Suggestions still point to albums already in your loaded library. The Last.fm
  preference, local-genre fallback and existing Open, Play and Queue controls
  remain available.

## Clearer update notes and incomplete-save feedback

- The update dialog now formats GitHub release notes with headings, lists,
  emphasis, code and simple tables. Links are restricted to HTTPS; embedded
  images and executable HTML are not loaded. Download progress preserves the
  notes' scroll position and keyboard focus.
- When a save creates an artist, uploads artwork or creates a split destination
  but cannot finish the next step, Tagcast reports the known creation or uncertain
  outcome in the result and Change history/export. It does not automatically
  delete those objects, roll back other changes or retry an uncertain write.
- Existing lyrics checks, combined-album editing restrictions and ordinary
  metadata review/read-back safeguards remain in place.

## Updating

Supported signed macOS apps and installed Debian/Ubuntu copies can offer the
update in Tagcast and install it after confirmation. Homebrew copies keep
`brew upgrade --cask tagcast`. Unsigned Windows, portable archives and source
installations retain their manual update routes.

macOS downloads cover Apple Silicon and Intel with Developer ID signing and
Apple notarization; Windows downloads remain unsigned. Package checksums accompany
the downloads. The [illustrated PDF manual](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/wiki/PDF-manual)
remains the 1.9.0 edition; the [Wiki](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/wiki)
describes the current controls.

Tagcast remains an independent app for iBroadcast. Existing local music files
are never retagged; explicit audio downloads create separate copies. Gapless
playback remains experimental, optional and off by default.
